newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan, U.S. to continue insurance talks - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan, U.S. to continue insurance talks - MOF.

text.p: Japan and the United States have made progress in trying to settle their dispute over the opening of Japan's insurance market to foreign companies, but more talks are needed and will continue on Saturday, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told reporters.

He made the remarks after he finished a meeting with Acting United States Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky in a last-ditch effort to resolve the dispute over the deregulation of the Japanese insurance market before a self-imposed Sunday deadline.
"We had meaningful discussions. I think we made good progress. We decided to talk on the phone later this evening," Mitsuzuka told reporters as he came out of the negotiations.
"We managed to narrow the gap from before, but our differences over basic issues still remain," he added.
Mitsuzuka said Japan had made some more proposals, based on those made in last ministerial meeting on December 7 and 8.
